thread:
jun_support: heads up — Acme prod is seeing a big spike of 503s on hosted inference starting ~12:15pm PDT. CS escalation from Acme; they report timeouts & retries, some billing retries. I can see a pattern of upstream worker exits and container restarts.

maria_sre: on it. do we have the runner logs and node events? any error class (OOM, segfault, driver)?

jun_support: pasting the relevant snippet from the runner logs (trimmed):
```
2026-03-17T19:15:08Z infer-runner[pid=4132]: ATTENTION_KERNEL: pmap: misaligned entry at 0x7f8c3b...
2026-03-17T19:15:08Z infer-runner[pid=4132]: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
2026-03-17T19:15:09Z containerd: infer-container exited with code 139, restarting
2026-03-17T19:15:09Z kubelet: pod "infer-abc-123" evicted, backoff restart
```
Not seeing a classic CUDA OOM message. memory usage for the pod at crash time was ~78% of GPU.

devon_eng: interesting — segfault + pmap misaligned suggests either driver/kernel-level corruption or a model runtime bug touching invalid memory (race after quant swap). which image + model variant?

jun_support: image: infer:v3.7-quantized. model: rdx-7b-quant-int8, context=4096, batch-size patterns show intermittent large requests with ~512 tokens. QPS ~18 on that pool.

maria_sre: can you confirm node driver versions and any recent deploys? I want to rule out kernel/driver mismatch.

devon_eng: checking node state — three nodes in hosted-gpu-pool-5 had driver updates yesterday (nvidia-driver 535.x). The container image was rolled 40m ago to v3.7-quantized (we did a canary earlier).

maria_sre: hypothesis: the quantized runtime path touched an uninitialized pointer under this driver version when handling KV cache prefetch for long contexts. Repro path: run rdx-7b-quant-int8 with long-context batch on a node with 535.x.

jun_support: CS asked for ETA. what's next mitigation?

oncall: applied temporary routing policy: shift 30% of traffic away from hosted-gpu-pool-5 to fallback pool (non-quantized variants) and increased min replicas for that pool. Draining pods on the three suspect nodes for now.

deploy-bot: rollback: starting rollout of infer:v3.6 (non-quant path) to hosted-gpu-pool-5 — staged canary -> 25% -> 100%.

devon_eng: recommended fix options: 1) immediate rollback to v3.6 non-quant (fast), 2) reproduce on a test node with driver 535 and run sanitizers (longer), 3) pin to older driver for pool (infra change). We'll start (1) now and run repro in parallel.

elaine_cs: told Acme we've routed traffic to a fallback model and are doing a rollback; asked them to retry and share any sample request IDs. They were appreciative, will ping if they see more 503s. :thumbsup:

jun_support: after routing + rollback the 503 rate dropped to baseline within ~90s for Acme. monitoring now.

maria_sre: follow-ups: - collect core dumps from the three drained nodes (enable CCC capture) - save full runner logs + model input that triggered crash - spin a repro cluster with driver 535 + v3.7-quant and run stress harness (seq len 512/1024).

devon_eng: added repro tasks to the board and assigned to me. I'll create a lightweight test that reproduces the pmap misalign and try ASAN builds.

oncall: keeping this open for 30m monitoring window. if 503s reappear we'll escalate to priority incident.

elaine_cs: Acme just replied: errors gone, thanks for quick action. requested postmortem and reassurance about billing retries (they saw 3 retries).

jun_support: noted — will coordinate billing note with finance and CS.

maria_sre: summary for postmortem: suspect interaction between quantized runtime and newer NVIDIA driver causing memory corruption -> SIGSEGV -> container restarts -> customer 503s. mitigation: rollback + route fallback. next steps: repro, driver compatibility test matrix, blocklist driver 535 for quantized images until fixed.

devon_eng: cc'ing runtime team for deeper debug. I'll drop follow-up with logs and repro steps in eng-runtime.

jun_support: closing for now; monitoring flag will be cleared at 19:45Z if stable. Thanks all.
